title: EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members
snippet: The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will both ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, not least war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.

title: France’s conundrum: How to cut spending amid protests
snippet: Prime Minister Lecornu is pledging to improve schools at a time when the government seeks to save billions. France's dilemma can be seen across the EU: How to cut spending when citizens are demanding more from the state?

title: Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia
snippet: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Some of these viral narratives are misleading.

title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
snippet: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
snippet: A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation.

title: Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
snippet: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

title: Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
snippet: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.

title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
snippet: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

title: UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
snippet: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

title: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
snippet: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

title: Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
snippet: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
snippet: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
snippet: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

title: EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
snippet: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.

title: Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
snippet: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

title: France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
snippet: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
snippet: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
snippet: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
snippet: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

title: Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
snippet: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.
